correctness.rationale: A closed H² fourth-order form with two bounded evaluations has the exact negative-inertia factorization through the positive free operator D⁴+1. The inverse kernel e^{-|x|/sqrt(2)}(cos+sin)/(2sqrt(2)) has the correct third-derivative unit jump. The two Birman–Schwinger eigenvalues yield a strict |F|>r criterion for exactly one negative eigenvalue in sqrt(2)<a<2sqrt(2). F'(t)=-2e^{-t}sin t, zeros (n+3/4)π and peaks e^{-nπ} give the exact count ceil(log(a/(2sqrt(2)-a))/π) and threshold equalities; neutral zero modes are distinguished from negative ones. Numerical checker 10079 checks independently compares Fourier integral and finite-difference negative mode counts. Infinite count rests on proof, not sampling.

value.rationale: The exact alternating stable/unstable separation windows are a structural consequence of the oscillatory fourth-order Green function, unlike monotone positive-kernel second-order interaction. The nontrivial component-count formula and infinitely many exponentially accumulating onset strengths solve a natural placement/stability classification for two individually subcritical destabilizing supports. Each additional window is a distinct separation regime, not an arbitrary numeric slice, and the result identifies precisely which negative stiffness strengths can produce any prescribed number of disconnected instability regions. Physical validity is limited to the defined linear idealization.
